# Rupert

- **Age:** nine  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034)</sub>
- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY STUBBS P12](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0012), [v5 CHAPTER VI. MARY STAYS AT THE MANSE P24](../source/v05-c06.md#nw-v05-c06-p0024)</sub>

## Appearance

Rupert features brown hair with a golden glint and dark-blue eyes inherited from his late mother. During an illness, he is noted to have flushed cheeks and a throbbing head.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE P29](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0029)_

## Personality

Rupert possesses a specialized knowledge of insects, feeling a close connection to creatures like beetles and bees. He is deeply considerate of his father, striving to suppress his own pain to avoid causing him distress, and is firmly determined to travel to the African jungles.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P8](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE P1](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER XXXIII. RUPERT IS—NOT—WHIPPED P27](../source/v05-c33.md#nw-v05-c33-p0027)_

## History

Rupert, whose real name was nine-year-old [Thomas](../character/thomas-sowerby.md) Carlyle, joined Tobias, [Grace](../character/grace.md), and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) in [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow) for a meal of cooked trout, where they quickly became fast friends with the [Carrow](../character/carrow.md) children. He later participated in harvesting potatoes from Evan Garrick's field, an act for which [Grace](../character/grace.md) took partial blame on his behalf in a local newspaper. While spending an evening at [Fern Hollow](../codex/places.md#fern-hollow), Rupert fled to [Hollowmere](../codex/places.md#hollowmere) with [Grace](../character/grace.md) and [Ida](../character/ida-ashdown.md) after being terrified by what they mistook for a ghost in the [Bailey](../codex/places.md#bailey) garden. As punishment for running away, Tobias forced Rupert to sit on a graveyard tombstone until midnight in chilly rain, causing Rupert to contract double pneumonia; after a grave battle, he eventually recovered. Later, Rupert threw an eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy, prompting his father to bring him to his study for a whipping, though his father relented at the last moment after seeing his late wife's eyes in the boy.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P34](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0034), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P37](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0037), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P45](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0045), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P46](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0046), [v5 CHAPTER IV. ### [John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/john-ashdown--rupert.md)

[John Ashdown](../character/john-ashdown.md) is Rupert's father. Their relationship faces tension due to Rupert's misbehavior, such as when Rupert throws an eel into Mrs. Carr's buggy. Although John intends to whip Rupert in his study for the incident, he relents at the last second upon seeing his late wife's eyes in the boy, leaving both of them shaken.
